articles.title: Relational databases
articles.brief: Understand shared relational facts, questions and guarded changes through one shop purchase. Distinguish schema rules, atomicity, concurrent decisions, query work and durability, judge relational fit and choose a practical next route.
articles.ownership_note: Introduce enough of each concern to choose a route; children own detailed design, formal analysis and working procedures.

articles.title: Relational data modelling
articles.brief: Design rows, keys and relationships that express the shop’s facts accurately. Diagnose dependencies and redundancy, distinguish historical facts from derived copies, and judge normalisation and modelling variations through required changes.

neighbouring_ownership.normalisation: Owns precise formal definitions, closure and decomposition methods.
neighbouring_ownership.hierarchies: Owns hierarchy representation comparisons and working maintenance procedures.
neighbouring_ownership.constraints: Owns enforcement, including subtype completeness and tenant references.
neighbouring_ownership.history: Owns temporal procedures; modelling establishes the difference between current and agreed price.

articles.title: Normalisation and decomposition
articles.brief: Derive candidate keys from declared dependencies and choose lossless, dependency-preserving decompositions where possible. Own closure, synthesis, 3NF versus BCNF, multivalued and join dependencies, and higher normal forms. The parent develops practical diagnoses and simple reconstruction examples.

neighbouring_ownership.data-modelling: Owns introductory anomalies, useful normal forms and the initial tags/suppliers and ternary offer contrasts.

articles.title: Modelling hierarchies
articles.brief: Choose and maintain trees or shared ancestry with adjacency lists, edge tables, paths, closure tables and nested sets. Compare traversal, reparenting, cycle prevention and consistency costs; the parent introduces recursive references and the tree-versus-multiple-parents decision.

neighbouring_ownership.query-results: Owns elementary joins; hierarchy traversal SQL, including recursive CTEs, belongs here.
neighbouring_ownership.constraints: Owns general enforcement choices; this article applies them to hierarchy consistency.

articles.title: Values, missing data and equality
articles.brief: Choose money, time, text and identity representations from their meanings. Reason about conversion, precision, collation, equality, ordering and NULL, including three-valued predicates and uniqueness edge cases.

neighbouring_ownership.query-results: Owns missing matches and the result grain.
neighbouring_ownership.data-modelling: Owns what a row asserts; values owns when an attribute is decomposed or represented as a structured value.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-json: Owns native JSONB operators, validation and indexing.

articles.title: Constraints and data integrity
articles.brief: Express identity, required values, row checks, references and exclusions in enforceable schema rules. Preserve tenant integrity with composite identities and references, and distinguish declarative enforcement, triggers and invariants needing a concurrency protocol.

neighbouring_ownership.access-control: Owns who may read or change rows.
neighbouring_ownership.transactions: Owns concurrent protocols for rules beyond declarative constraints.
neighbouring_ownership.history: Owns correction and deletion policy; constraints applies that policy to references.

articles.title: History, correction and deletion
articles.brief: Represent agreements and changing facts with explicit effective and recorded times. Carry corrections, retention and deletion through related and external records without rewriting the meaning of historical purchases.

neighbouring_ownership.data-modelling: Owns first current-price versus agreed-price distinction.
neighbouring_ownership.backups: Owns restoring an earlier database history and reconciling valid work.

articles.title: Joins and the meaning of a result row
articles.brief: Build SELECT and JOIN results with deliberate row meaning. Predict multiplicity and missing matches, use existence tests, distinguish compatible-row set operations and their duplicates from joining columns, and complete the still-due report by summarising lines and payments separately per order.

neighbouring_ownership.aggregation: Owns general grouping, HAVING, FILTER, empty/count distinctions and windows; query results owns only the narrow per-order GROUP BY/SUM summary required for its report.
neighbouring_ownership.query-execution: Owns physical join methods and execution order.

articles.ownership_note: Own compact UNION ALL/UNION duplicate semantics and orientation to INTERSECT/EXCEPT; no separate thin child.

articles.title: Aggregates and window functions
articles.brief: Choose grouped or per-row calculations without losing the intended grain. Own general GROUP BY, HAVING, FILTER, empty inputs and counts, deterministic ordering, ranking, peers and window frames.

neighbouring_ownership.query-results: Owns its single per-order SUM/GROUP BY report repair; this article develops the general methods.
neighbouring_ownership.pagination: Owns stable cursor keys and changing-result continuation.
neighbouring_ownership.query-execution: Owns physical aggregate and sort work.

articles.title: Pagination and consistent exports
articles.brief: Choose a continuation contract for a changing list and a snapshot contract for an export. Build keyset cursors that preserve ties and explain omissions, duplicates, retention and cancellation costs.

neighbouring_ownership.indexes: Owns efficient index support; pagination owns cursor correctness.
neighbouring_ownership.application-sql: Owns driver result streaming and cancellation mechanics.

articles.title: Updates, upserts and bulk imports
articles.brief: Make changes conditional and interpret affected rows. Choose conflict meaning for an upsert and stage, validate and reconcile replayable batches, including a rejected row and a partially processed import.

neighbouring_ownership.transactions: Owns one-row and multi-row concurrent invariant protocols.
neighbouring_ownership.retry-outcomes: Owns one logical request across unknown commit outcomes.
neighbouring_ownership.schema-change: Owns backfill convergence while callers keep writing.
neighbouring_ownership.application-sql: Owns connection, parameter and failure plumbing.

articles.title: SQL at the application boundary
articles.brief: Preserve query meaning and transaction ownership across drivers, pools and ORMs. Separate parameters from SQL structure, map results, bound repeated queries, and handle one request’s connection, error and cancellation coherently.

neighbouring_ownership.capacity: Owns pool sizing, admission and overload.
neighbouring_ownership.outboxes-jobs: Owns durable external intentions and worker recovery.
neighbouring_ownership.access-control: Owns authority of application and administrative identities.

articles.title: Transactions and isolation
articles.brief: Choose atomic work and isolation from the invariant being preserved. Distinguish committed visibility, statement and transaction snapshots and serial outcomes; develop sound one-row stock and multi-row capacity protocols.

neighbouring_ownership.locks: Owns explicit lock scope, ordering and wait diagnosis.
neighbouring_ownership.storage-durability: Owns how versions and logs implement physical history, without treating storage versions as business history.

articles.title: Locks, contention and deadlocks
articles.brief: Choose a lockable authority and a sound isolation and snapshot protocol for a decision. Design lock scope and acquisition order, then diagnose deadlocks and bound waiting without weakening the invariant.

neighbouring_ownership.transactions: Owns isolation-level reasoning; locks develops protocols and contention.
neighbouring_ownership.incidents: Owns deciding whether blocked work explains the request symptom.

articles.title: Retries and uncertain commit outcomes
articles.brief: Distinguish a known abort from a commit whose reply was lost. Reuse one logical request identity, reject conflicting payloads, and recover the recorded result rather than applying a purchase twice.

neighbouring_ownership.outboxes-jobs: Owns external delivery and worker identity.
neighbouring_ownership.application-sql: Owns error transport and connection disposal.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-transactions: Owns native retry and ambiguous-result errors.

articles.title: Outboxes and database-backed jobs
articles.brief: Commit a durable intention with the domain change, then deliver or claim work despite duplicate execution and worker loss. Design deduplication, leases, expiry and fencing so recovery preserves the intended external effects.

neighbouring_ownership.locks: Owns general locking; this article applies claiming mechanisms.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-logical-replication: Owns native row-change streams rather than application outbox semantics.

articles.title: Query execution and performance
articles.brief: Follow rows through scans, joins, grouping and sorting. Use measured plans to locate bad cardinality estimates, repeated work, spills and data movement; test a repair against realistic parameters and workload.

neighbouring_ownership.indexes: Owns access-path design, not all query repair.
neighbouring_ownership.incidents: Owns separating execution work from admission and lock waits.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-plans: Owns native PostgreSQL counters and plan behaviour.

articles.title: Indexes and access paths
articles.brief: Derive useful index keys, ranges, ordering and covering from a query and the distribution of values. Compare pages and rows examined with rows returned, then weigh write, space and maintenance costs across the workload.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-indexes: Owns PostgreSQL methods, operator classes and rechecks.
neighbouring_ownership.schema-change: Owns compatible rollout, including index changes.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-schema-change: Owns PostgreSQL build validity and native concurrent maintenance procedures.

articles.title: Table partitioning and data lifecycle
articles.brief: Choose a partition boundary for useful pruning or retention without assuming it distributes work across servers. Derive pruning from predicates and account for global identity, references and safe partition retirement.

articles.title: Storage and durability
articles.brief: Connect logical updates to pages, buffers, retained row versions and cleanup, distinguishing reusable space, file shrinkage and write amplification. Explain write-ahead ordering, commit durability and restart recovery, and separate them from recovery after lost storage or an unwanted committed change.

neighbouring_ownership.backups: Owns restorable history and recovery reconciliation.
neighbouring_ownership.replicas: Owns copied history, progress and read routing.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-vacuum: Owns native retention diagnosis and transaction age.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-wal: Owns native settings and crash drills.

articles.title: Backup, restore and reconciliation
articles.brief: Choose and verify a restorable history from recovery-point and recovery-time needs. Test the backup chain and restore target, close the source history, and reconcile valid later work and external effects without duplicate application.

neighbouring_ownership.history: Owns business correction rather than database restore.
neighbouring_ownership.failover: Owns transfer to an existing live copy.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-backup: Owns native base backup and WAL procedures.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-backup: Owns native backup coverage and restore scope.

articles.title: Replicas, lag and read routing
articles.brief: Trace copied history through received, durable and replayed progress. Choose read routing from freshness and failure promises, including read-your-write needs, stale reads and log retention.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-replication: Owns native standby controls and measurements.
neighbouring_ownership.distribution: Owns quorum-based agreement within one replicated partition; this article owns copied-history progress and read routing.

articles.title: Failover and fencing
articles.brief: Distinguish suspected failure from authority to write. Fence a former writer, choose a promotion point with an explicit loss boundary, reconcile divergence and rejoin safely.

neighbouring_ownership.cluster-change: Owns replicated membership and planned data movement, not primary/standby promotion.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-replication: Owns native physical promotion and return.

articles.title: Diagnosing a database incident
articles.brief: Start with a slow or failing request and use evidence to distinguish pool delay, lock waits, expensive execution and storage pressure. Choose a bounded intervention and account for its recovery cost.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-operations: Owns PostgreSQL evidence and native intervention.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-operations: Owns native cluster health and secure operation.

articles.title: Live schema changes and backfills
articles.brief: Move through compatible schema and caller states using expand, migrate and contract. Prove a backfill converged despite races and late rows, and define acceptance and return boundaries.

neighbouring_ownership.writes: Owns import mechanics outside a live compatibility protocol.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-schema-change: Owns PostgreSQL locks, rewrites and index validity.

articles.title: Connections, overload and capacity
articles.brief: Distinguish connections, active work and queued requests, then budget admitted work and recovery headroom around the real limiting resource. Choose bounded overload behaviour and validate capacity under a representative workload.

neighbouring_ownership.application-sql: Owns the lifecycle of an individual connection.
neighbouring_ownership.cluster-change: Owns temporary capacity and redundancy consumed by movement.

articles.title: Database access and least privilege
articles.brief: Derive runtime, migration and support privileges from their tasks. Test tenant access as the actual trusted identity, distinguishing database authorisation, application identity and row-level integrity.

neighbouring_ownership.constraints: Owns tenant integrity and composite references.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-access: Owns native roles, row policies and privileged code.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-operations: Owns native CockroachDB secure identities and privileges.

articles.title: Sharding and distributed SQL
articles.brief: Choose a distribution boundary from local work, invariant scope and the actual bottleneck. Distinguish replicas from shards, explain authoritative replicated history, acknowledgements and quorum availability, and separate agreement within one partition from atomic commit across partitions. Derive locality, skew, fan-out and coordination from the key.

neighbouring_ownership.placement: Owns latency and survival across failure domains.
neighbouring_ownership.replicas: Owns copied-history progress and read routing; distribution establishes quorum-based agreement within one replicated partition.

articles.title: Transactions across partitions
articles.brief: Explain atomic outcomes across partitions, including recovery of a distributed decision after coordinator loss. Distinguish replica agreement from transaction commit and connect invariant scope to the participants that must coordinate.

neighbouring_ownership.crdb-transactions: Owns CockroachDB intents, transaction records and native error contracts.
neighbouring_ownership.distribution: Establishes authoritative replicated history, acknowledgement guarantees and losing-quorum availability before this article uses replica agreement.

articles.title: Time, snapshots and distributed reads
articles.brief: Read related partitions at a safe common history. Compare logical timestamps, clock uncertainty and safe historical reads while distinguishing a past observation from authority for a current decision.

neighbouring_ownership.replicas: Owns single-copy read routing and read-your-write needs.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-reads: Owns native isolation and follower-read choices.

articles.title: Regional placement and survival
articles.brief: Place data and voting replicas against stated latency and survival needs. Derive quorum survival from failure domains and trace the remote coordination introduced by apparently local data and global invariants.

neighbouring_ownership.cluster-change: Owns changing membership and placement safely.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-locality: Owns native table-locality and survival settings.
neighbouring_ownership.distribution: Establishes authoritative replicated history, acknowledgement guarantees and losing-quorum availability before this article uses replica agreement.

articles.title: Rebalancing and cluster change
articles.brief: Move replicas and data while preserving authoritative history. Explain catch-up and safe membership change, and budget rebalancing and decommissioning without treating lost redundancy as spare capacity.

neighbouring_ownership.crdb-operations: Owns native node removal and health evidence.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-upgrades: Owns binary rollout and finalised cluster version.
neighbouring_ownership.distribution: Establishes authoritative replicated history, acknowledgement guarantees and losing-quorum availability before this article uses replica agreement.

articles.title: Inside PostgreSQL
articles.brief: Trace one connection and request through PostgreSQL processes, shared buffers, heap tuples and indexes. Explain tuple visibility, HOT updates and their physical limits so native plans and maintenance have a concrete physical setting.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-vacuum: Owns retained horizons and transaction-age maintenance.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-wal: Owns durability controls and crash drills.

articles.title: PostgreSQL vacuum and transaction age
articles.brief: Diagnose retained PostgreSQL versions, visibility and transaction-age risk before changing maintenance. Distinguish reusable space from bloat and file shrinkage; choose vacuum and related interventions from retained horizons and age evidence.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-architecture: Owns first visibility and HOT explanation.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-replication: Owns standby and slot retention policy.

articles.title: PostgreSQL index methods and operators
articles.brief: Choose a PostgreSQL access method and operator class from the operator’s meaning and data organisation. Compare B-tree, hash, GIN, GiST, SP-GiST and BRIN, and verify candidates, rechecks and write costs in native plans.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-schema-change: Owns concurrent builds, invalid indexes and native maintenance procedures.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-text: Owns linguistic text retrieval and ranking.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-extensions: Owns specialised type and extension dependencies.

articles.title: Reading and repairing PostgreSQL plans
articles.brief: Interpret EXPLAIN ANALYZE counters without confusing estimates, per-loop work, buffers or timings. Test statistics, access paths and prepared-plan repairs under skew and workload variation.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-indexes: Owns native method and operator semantics.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-operations: Owns waits and admission outside plan execution.

articles.title: PostgreSQL JSON and structured alternatives
articles.brief: Choose columns, related rows or JSONB from the facts, validation and update boundary. Match native JSON operators and indexes while preserving established identities, types and data rules.

neighbouring_ownership.data-modelling: Owns introductory JSON versus tables versus EAV judgement.
neighbouring_ownership.values: Owns general equality and value representation.

articles.title: PostgreSQL WAL, checkpoints and durability
articles.brief: Interpret PostgreSQL WAL progress, checkpoint work and commit settings against a tested durability promise. Explain an isolated crash drill and its restart evidence without extrapolating to power loss or lost storage.

neighbouring_ownership.storage-durability: Owns general mechanism and failure distinctions.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-backup: Owns backup chains, targets and restore.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-replication: Owns standby progress and synchronous-copy promises.

articles.title: Restoring PostgreSQL to a recovery target
articles.brief: Build and test a base-backup and archived-WAL chain, restore a verified target and account for valid work outside the recovered history. Close source writes before reconciliation and preserve external-effect identity.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-replication: Owns promoting an existing physical copy.

articles.title: PostgreSQL physical replicas and promotion
articles.brief: Operate a physical standby with separate receipt, flush and replay evidence. Choose synchronous promises, perform fenced promotion with an explicit loss boundary, and return a former primary safely.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-logical-replication: Owns selective row streams and their separate lifecycle.

articles.title: PostgreSQL logical replication and change feeds
articles.brief: Configure a publication and subscriber with deliberate replica identity. Treat the stream as selective row changes, accounting for schema, sequences, lag, retained log and cutover responsibilities.

neighbouring_ownership.outboxes-jobs: Owns durable application intentions and delivery semantics.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-upgrades: Owns full migration acceptance and write handover.

articles.title: PostgreSQL schema changes under load
articles.topic: PostgreSQL live schema and index work
articles.brief: Choose native schema and index operations from their lock, rewrite and validity behaviour. Bound waits, validate backfill convergence and maintain indexes without accepting incomplete semantic or physical work.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-indexes: Owns which access method serves the query.

articles.title: Operating and diagnosing PostgreSQL
articles.brief: Trace a request through pool and server evidence to distinguish blocked work, excessive execution and connection pressure. Test a targeted intervention with bounded waits and account for recovery costs.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-vacuum: Owns version retention and age repair.

articles.title: PostgreSQL roles, policies and privileged code
articles.brief: Test role inheritance, ownership and row-policy boundaries as the actual application identities. Explain bypass cases and secure privileged routines against identity and name-resolution mistakes.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-extensions: Owns extension installation and lifecycle privileges.

articles.title: Upgrading and migrating PostgreSQL
articles.brief: Choose between a major upgrade and a logical migration, then rehearse compatibility, a recoverable write handover and acceptance. Identify the point after which a simple return is no longer possible.

neighbouring_ownership.crdb-migration: Owns the PostgreSQL-to-CockroachDB application contract transfer.

articles.title: Distributing PostgreSQL work
articles.brief: Choose among native partitions, application shards, Citus and foreign tables from co-location, invariant scope and movement needs. Derive local work, skew and fan-out, then preserve single ownership through a transfer.

neighbouring_ownership.partitioning: Owns native table-pruning and lifecycle concepts.

articles.title: Full-text search in PostgreSQL
articles.brief: Build text retrieval from tokens, phrases and configuration through ranked, filtered results. Keep indexed candidate retrieval, linguistic matching and relevance evaluation distinct, including maintenance when source text or configuration changes.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-vector: Owns embedding-vector retrieval; text relevance is not nearest-neighbour recall.

articles.title: Vector search in PostgreSQL
articles.brief: Evaluate vector retrieval independently from the embedding model’s semantic usefulness. Compare exact, HNSW and IVFFlat retrieval under filtering, nearest-neighbour recall, latency and index lifecycle costs.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-text: Owns linguistic matching and lexical ranking.
neighbouring_ownership.pg-extensions: Owns shared installation, restore and upgrade dependency handling.

articles.title: Types and extensions in PostgreSQL
articles.topic: PostgreSQL specialised types and extension lifecycle
articles.brief: Express overlap and spatial predicates with suitable types, operators and indexes. Own extension installation, privileges, dependencies, restore, upgrade and removal, including when an extension becomes part of the application’s durability contract.

neighbouring_ownership.pg-vector: Owns complete vector retrieval and evaluation.

articles.title: Inside CockroachDB
articles.brief: Trace SQL data through ordered keys, ranges, local storage and replicated ownership. Explain splits, leases and replica agreement with enough detail to see why a hotspot can persist as a cluster grows.

neighbouring_ownership.crdb-transactions: Owns native intents and commit/retry paths.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-performance: Owns SQL/KV/network work and hot-range diagnosis.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-operations: Owns health, identity and removal procedures.
neighbouring_ownership.distribution: Owns transferable replica-agreement concepts; this article develops their native range, Raft and lease application.

articles.title: CockroachDB transactions and retries
articles.brief: Relate intents and transaction state to atomic visibility, then handle native transaction retry and ambiguous-result paths for one logical purchase. Preserve the request identity and keep external work outside a replayed transaction.

neighbouring_ownership.transactions: Owns general invariant and isolation reasoning.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-reads: Owns current versus historical read choices.

articles.title: CockroachDB isolation and follower reads
articles.brief: Choose Serializable, Read Committed and historical reads from the decision they must support. Explain safe follower reads, freshness and retention limits without treating a historical observation as current authority.

articles.title: CockroachDB query work and hot ranges
articles.brief: Locate lookups, fan-out, SQL/KV work, network movement and contention from native evidence. Weigh covering and distributed keys against write and ordering costs, and separate less work from a hot-key bottleneck.

neighbouring_ownership.query-execution: Owns general execution operators and repairs.

articles.title: CockroachDB table locality and region survival
articles.brief: Choose regional-by-table, regional-by-row or GLOBAL tables and survival goals from actual access and failure requirements. Verify placement and survival, and distinguish structural reasoning from measured regional latency.

neighbouring_ownership.crdb-operations: Owns native health and planned node removal.

articles.title: Operating and securing a CockroachDB cluster
articles.brief: Verify secure runtime identity, least privilege and tenant isolation. Use native evidence to diagnose under-replication and range health, then remove a node without consuming the cluster’s survival budget.

neighbouring_ownership.crdb-performance: Owns expensive query and hot-key repairs.
neighbouring_ownership.cluster-change: Owns general movement and membership safety.

articles.title: CockroachDB backup and recovery
articles.brief: Validate full and incremental backup coverage and restore scope. Restore the intended history, close source writes, and reconcile valid later work by identity and external effects without charging again or repeating its stock consumption.

neighbouring_ownership.backups: Owns general recovery and reconciliation method.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-migration: Owns a whole application write handover.

articles.title: CockroachDB schema jobs under load
articles.brief: Treat schema changes as observable jobs inside an application compatibility protocol. Interpret progress, failure and cleanup, and accept a backfill or unique index only after semantic checks.

neighbouring_ownership.crdb-upgrades: Owns binary compatibility rather than application schema jobs.

articles.title: Upgrading a CockroachDB cluster
articles.brief: Rehearse binary rollout and the cluster-version boundary. Distinguish mixed binaries from finalised compatibility, and verify application acceptance, rollback eligibility and recovery choices.

neighbouring_ownership.cluster-change: Owns general redundancy and movement budgets.
neighbouring_ownership.crdb-migration: Owns application transfer between database systems.

articles.title: Moving a SQL application to CockroachDB
articles.brief: Find semantic incompatibilities behind similar SQL, then port the application contract. Validate a consistent copy, transfer one write authority and reconcile a return path with explicit limits once new writes are accepted.

neighbouring_ownership.crdb-backup: Owns native backup and restore scope.

proposed_boundary_changes.change: Merge generic storage and crash recovery
proposed_boundary_changes.reason: One change can connect physical versions, buffers, log ordering and crash survival without repeating a second account of pages and commit. Preserve all listed outcomes and retain deeper native procedures.
Practical modelling remains useful without formal decomposition or hierarchy-maintenance procedures.

Generic articles teach transferable mechanisms and judgement; native articles own version-specific evidence, behaviour and working procedures. A native article is entered by prerequisite concepts, not by completing the generic collection.
